what_happened: Discovered the merge engine already has a tested retraction primitive (M.unmerge_settings + build_retained_fragments + state.get_merged_sections) and a load-time hook-orphan-sweep precedent (task 369), both unused by the forced-reload/resync_all path. Recommending a small sequencing fix (call existing unmerge before re-merge in manager.load's force branch) instead of a new permissions-specific mechanism or a one-time migration script, since deploy-headless.sh's TARGET_REPO argument + nvim's fixed runtime config location means the single engine fix propagates to all five named repos via redeploy alone.

Research report cited the sapience tracked-record jq path as .extensions.sapience.merged_sections.settings.permissions.allow.items; the actual path carries a 'children' level (settings.permissions.children.allow.items). A filter copied from the report's prose returns empty. Substantive claim (7 tracked items vs 11 deployed) confirmed. Correction recorded in the plan's Premise Re-Validation table.

validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification measurement check caught a genuinely fabricated suite claim: Phase 4 named test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh, but suite_selection_select over that phase's FOUR-path union returns __FULL_SWEEP__ (a single uncovered path forces the sentinel). Per-file selector output is not composable into a per-phase claim; the union must be measured. Fixed before the plan was accepted.

Phase 2's planned mechanism (unmerge the extension's prior tracked merged_sections, then re-merge the current fragment) is a correct general fix but CANNOT retroactively remediate the five already-affected repositories: git history confirms a routine redeploy already reset this repo's sapience tracked record from 11 to 7 items (commit 94b181040) before this task began, well after the fragment was narrowed (commit 0564e2554). state.mark_loaded overwrites merged_sections wholesale on every load, so the wide historical tracked record no longer exists anywhere on disk in any of the five repos. Confirmed empirically: applying only the planned unmerge-then-remerge retraction against a scratch fixture reproducing the real drift (narrow tracked record, wide deployed file) left the deployed grant count unchanged at 11. Added a second, complementary mechanism -- an MCP-permission-grant orphan sweep (merge_mod.remove_orphaned_mcp_permission_grants/restore_removed_mcp_permission_grants, build_permission_valid_set in init.lua) modeled directly on the existing hook-registration orphan sweep -- which reasons from currently-loaded extensions' CURRENT fragments rather than historical tracked data, and does correctly converge the fixture to exactly 7 grants with a byte-identical hooks fingerprint. Both mechanisms are kept: the tracked-record retraction for other merge-target categories and future narrowings, the orphan sweep for this specific already-lost-history case.

Scratch-fixture smoke test confirms the combined fix (tracked-record retraction + MCP-permission-grant orphan sweep) converges a drifted 11-grant deployed settings.local.json to exactly the 7 read-shaped sapience grants on a forced reload, leaves the hooks fingerprint byte-identical, is idempotent on a repeat forced reload, and still yields exactly 7 grants on a genuine first-time load into a never-loaded fixture.

Phase 3's planned rollback-integration case (a forced load made to fail after the retraction, exercised through manager.load's own pcall, asserting the retracted entries are restored) was deferred: engineering a genuine mid-pcall failure inside manager.load from a black-box bash integration harness has no monkeypatch seam, and was judged disproportionate to this task's remaining budget. The restore primitives (merge_mod.restore_retracted_sections, merge_mod.restore_removed_mcp_permission_grants) are directly unit-tested for correctness in isolation in merge_spec.lua; only the manager.load WIRING that calls them on load_ok==false (confirmed correct by code inspection during Phase 2) remains integration-untested.
